description.value: The study examined whether the first behavioral symptom of bvFTD, apathy or disinhibition, is associated with later neuropsychological and brain-atrophy profiles and can distinguish patient subgroups.

design.value: A retrospective, cross-sectional comparison of healthy controls and two groups of patients with probable bvFTD defined by their first reported symptom, with neuropsychological assessment and 3T structural MRI performed approximately three years after disease debut. Group differences were assessed with neuropsychological, whole-brain VBM, ROI, correlation, discriminant-analysis, and support-vector-machine methods.

task_description.value: Neurocognitive processes were evaluated with a standardized neuropsychological measures typically used in patients with neurodegenerative diseases.

instrument.value: Philips Achieva 3T scanner with a 16-channel SENSE antenna

description.value: The anatomical and 3D T1-weighted images had TR = 7.9, TE = 3.8, ACQ matrix 220×220 pixels, voxel size 0.5×0.5×0.5 mm, and 310 sections.

The T1-weighted images were normalized to the same stereotaxic space generated from the complete data set using the DARTEL algorithm. The images were segmented into WM and GM and non-brain voxels (CSF, skull), modulated to correct volume changes by Jacobian determinants, and smoothed by convolution with an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 8-mm full-width at half maximum.

steps.value: Each image was inspected for artifacts.

All images were modulated to correct volume changes by Jacobian determinants.
Images were smoothed by convolution with an isotropic Gaussian kernel of 8-mm full-width at half maximum.

model_settings.value: Whole brain analyses compared AbvFTD and DbvFTD groups with healthy controls, controlling for global intracranial volume, age, gender and length of disease duration. Whole-brain and ROI analyses were corrected using FDR at 0.001 and 0.05, respectively.

software.value: VBM8 in the Statistical Parametric Mapping 8 package (SPM8), running under Matlab 2012b

model_settings.value: Multiple correlations were performed between VBM scores in ROIs and standardized scores of neuropsychological measures in each group, with Sidak correction.

Two FDA models were performed: one including significant neuropsychological and anatomical variables and a second including only significant anatomical variables. A final stepwise discriminant analysis was performed at the 5% level.

estimator.value: stepwise discriminant analysis; individual predictive scores were examined by t-test

model_settings.value: The optimal values of γ, the width of the radial basis function, and C, the error/trade-off parameter, were determined. Recursive feature elimination was used for feature selection, and SVM models were implemented with 10-fold cross validation.
